subject.title: Feishu: duplicate final replies can occur after model failover from rate-limited primary

question: Should this be fixed as a Feishu-local recovery guard, a shared same-turn final identity contract, or folded into the broader durable final-delivery contract?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally preserve later finals after an error closeout, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent behavior boundary without risking either duplicate Feishu replies or suppressed legitimate recovery output.

options.title: Narrow Feishu Recovery Guard
options.body: Make Feishu keep, replace, or withdraw the errored-attempt card during transient failure and deliver only the recovered fallback final for that user turn, with explicit exceptions for distinct diagnostics.

options.title: Shared Final Identity Contract
options.body: Define dispatcher-level same-turn final identity so channels can collapse failed-attempt and recovered-fallback duplicates while preserving intentionally distinct finals.

options.title: Fold Into Durable Delivery Roadmap
options.body: Track this only under the broader durable final-delivery contract and defer a Feishu-local fix until that cross-channel contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Narrow Feishu Recovery Guard
recommendation.body: Make Feishu keep, replace, or withdraw the errored-attempt card during transient failure and deliver only the recovered fallback final for that user turn, with explicit exceptions for distinct diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current routing candidate from Feishu reply-dispatch and release-history evidence around this surface.
